correctness.rationale: For every proposed selected set, the selected edge-vertices must form an edge cover because original vertices have no original-vertex neighbors. Once this is so, the unselected edge-vertices have an incident selected edge-vertex; a selected edge-vertex is dominated except when its original edge is isolated in the cover. Exactly those pairwise disjoint isolated edges force nonempty endpoint choices. This proves the full polynomial factorization. In the signed multivariate expression, a free original vertex cancels by toggling it; a cover with no free original vertices is exactly a perfect matching, and the sign per matched pair is -1 canceled by its selected edge-vertex sign. This yields unit coefficient at each perfect-matching monomial and zero elsewhere. Isolated original vertices give no feasible sets and no perfect matching. The supplied independent direct-definition enumeration tests 725 small labeled graphs and 1,246,184 candidate subsets, including nonconnected cases; the infinite proof does not rely on the finite tests.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of the combinatorial statements with the inspected arXiv full texts found no counting formula for all total dominating sets of middle graphs and no signed multivariate perfect-matching sieve. The 2022 paper studies the minimum cardinality and graph-family bounds; the 2016 paper gives general recurrence formulas and evaluations for other graph classes. The 2025 open-neighborhood hypergraph article gives general transversal equivalence and particular tree enumerations but no middle-graph or perfect-matching identity. Separate research-record searches on both the original formulation and algebraically equivalent parity-signed and edge-cover statements found different invariants or transforms, not a dominating theorem. Novelty remains best-knowledge rather than a proof of absolute priority.

value.rationale: An unexpected identity connects two different all-graph invariants: a signed total domination generating function of the middle graph and the perfect-matching polynomial of the original graph, with coefficientwise support and positivity as direct consequences. It holds without connectivity or planarity assumptions, and its elementary involutive cancellation provides a reusable structural tool; it is not an arbitrary finite census or a renamed minimum number. The ordinary complete polynomial edge-cover expansion independently refines all cardinalities, though direct evaluation can be exponentially costly.
